Let me reconcile the findings with one real constraint the review understates: **DTO Bean Validation runs on the raw payload before the mapper**, so I can't both strip in the mapper *and* keep a strict digit-only schema pattern — the raw `(04) 1234-5678` has separators. The reconciliation that satisfies all four findings is a declarative schema pattern that asserts "exactly 10 digits, ignoring separators," which flows through the normal `MethodArgumentNotValidException` → `ExceptionControllerAdvice` 400 path, plus digit-stripping moved into the mapper.

Now let me revert the controller `addOwner` to a thin pass-through, and make `updateOwner` reuse the shared normalizer for consistency:

components:
  schemas:
    ProblemDetail:
      title: Problem Detail
      description: The schema for all error responses.
      type: object
      properties:
        type:
          title: Type
          description: Full URL that originated the error response.
          type: string
          format: uri
          example: 'http://localhost:9966/petclinic/api/owner'
          readOnly: true
        title:
          title: Title
          description: The short error title.
          type: string
          example: NoResourceFoundException
          readOnly: true
        status:
          title: Status
          description: HTTP status code
          type: integer
          format: int32
          minimum: 400
          maximum: 600
          exclusiveMaximum: true
          example: 500
          readOnly: true
        detail:
          title: Detail
          description: The long error message.
          type: string
          example: 'No static resource api/owner.'
          readOnly: true
        timestamp:
          title: Timestamp
          description: The time the error occurred.
          type: string
          format: date-time
          example: '2024-11-23T13:59:21.3820407Z'
          readOnly: true
        schemaValidationErrors:
          title: Schema validation errors
          description: Validation errors against the OpenAPI schema.
          type: array
          items:
            $ref: '#/components/schemas/ValidationMessage'
      required:
        - type
        - title
        - status
        - detail
        - timestamp
        - schemaValidationErrors
    ValidationMessage:
      title: Validation message
      description: Messages describing a validation error.
      type: object
      properties:
        message:
          title: Message
          description: The validation message.
          type: string
          example: "[Path '/lastName'] Instance type (null) does not match any allowed primitive type (allowed: ['string'])"
          readOnly: true
      required:
        - message
      additionalProperties: true
    Specialty:
      title: Specialty
      description: Fields of specialty of vets.
      type: object
      properties:
        id:
          title: ID
          description: The ID of the specialty.
          type: integer
          format: int32
          minimum: 0
          example: 1
          readOnly: true
        name:
          title: Name
          description: The name of the specialty.
          type: string
          maxLength: 80
          minLength: 1
          example: radiology
      required:
        - id
        - name
    OwnerFields:
      title: Owner fields
      description: Editable fields of a pet owner.
      type: object
      properties:
        firstName:
          title: First name
          description: The first name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}$"
          example: George
        lastName:
          title: Last name
          description: The last name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}\\.?$"
          example: Franklin
        address:
          title: Address
          description: The postal address of the pet owner.
          type: string

I agreed with the thrust of all four findings and restructured accordingly, with one reconciliation the review needed.

**Findings 1 & 2 (ad-hoc 400 / fat controller) — fixed.** `addOwner` is back to a thin pass-through (`map → saveOwner → map back`), identical in shape to its siblings. I also made `updateOwner` call the same shared normalizer, so the two endpoints stay consistent (and update no longer risks a 500 against the entity's `^[0-9]{10}$` constraint when given separators).

**Finding 4 (abandoned declarative validation) — fixed, with a correction.** I restored a schema `pattern` on `telephone`. But the review's literal suggestion — a strict digit pattern like `^[0-9]{10}$` — can't work: DTO Bean Validation runs on the **raw** payload *before* the mapper, so a strict digit-only pattern would reject `(04) 1234-5678` before normalization ever happens, breaking the accepted-input case. The pattern `^\D*(\d\D*){10}$` expresses the real rule declaratively — "exactly 10 digits, tolerating separators that normalization strips" — and is enforced/reported through the standard path.

The clean MapStruct idiom here is `@Named` + `qualifiedByName`, **not** a plain `default String→String` helper. A plain default method gets auto-selected by MapStruct for *every* String property, so `toOwner` initially stripped `firstName`/`city`/etc. too (turning `"Test"` into `""` → `@NotEmpty` failure → 500). `@Named` keeps it out of automatic selection; I verified the generated `OwnerMapperImpl` now normalizes telephone only.
